children: OQ, Oman’s global energy investment group, has signed preliminary agreements to explore opportunities in Angola’s energy sector, including upstream exploration and green energy.

The company has signed with Angola’s state-owned oil company Sonangol to identify and assess potential areas of cooperation, including upstream exploration and production, liquefied natural gas (LNG), fertilisers, gas monetisation opportunities including ammonia and petrochemicals and the potential supply and purchase of commodities, it said in a press statement.

OQ Alternative Energy, an OQ subsidiary, also signed a memorandum with Angola’s Ministry of Energy and Water to evaluate and advance the potential development of 500 megawatts of renewable energy generation, alongside a battery energy storage system, through an independent power producer (IPP) commercial model.
OQ operates in 17 countries and has a commercial presence in Africa through its subsidiaries.

title: Oman's OQ evaluates plans to invest in Angola's energy sector
